notes.title: A sneaky little Las Vegas peek!
notes.content:
[p]Hey Hoteliers, [/p][p] We know you're all eagerly waiting on a date for the release of the Las Vegas and casinos update, and we'll be able to give you that very soon! 

Today we've got a little sneak preview of what you can expect in the update, and while not everything is in these shots, there's plenty to look at! This way you'll be able to start planning how you want to lay out your casinos and new hotels 😊  

Las Vegas as a map will be 18 x 18 across 8 floors, so that's even bigger than New York with 2592 tiles. It's a huge amount of space to build in and you could possibly have a floor with a mega casino in if you wanted. We're also including 3 financial starting options again for those that like more of a challenge!  

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/8d289ca0684505b937d28a6f3a8679824c7a147e.png"][/img][/p][p]The casino zone can be any shape/size that you would like and you can even place it around a bar zone which would be quite fitting. 

You can have multiples of each table, but remember you will need to have staff to cover them all if its suddenly busy. Croupiers are the new staff type coming with the update and they can move between types of table. If one has guests waiting but their current one doesn't, they will head over to run the game. 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/0f5a7b5c39520a83013a60ef52fd48c6fa6b409d.png"][/img][/p][p]Casinos can contain a variety of 5 types of casino tables - roulette, blackjack, baccarat, craps and a fortune wheel, plus 3 versions of slot machines for your casinos.   

Each requires a cash deposit and must stay above a certain threshold to remain operational and you’ll need to tailor bet sizes to suit your guest types, just like you do with your guest rooms. 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/b64e566c36e3637f6035d65a895d046e0face3b4.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re also rolling out a bunch of new furniture and items to help you capture that iconic Vegas atmosphere! Think glitz, glamour, and a touch of extravagance.. or just a fancy car on show in the middle of the room if you want. [/p][p]Your casinos can be overwhelmingly with bright light pillars and noise or a more dialled back and sophisticated vibe, you decide![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/fd7ca4585bda21ee2dd1a00c48d8479e0e1ac546.png"][/img] 

So what do you think? We hope you're excited and we'll have more news for you soon!   

- The Hotel Architect Team[/p]

notes.title: Our Top Tips for building in New York!
notes.content:
[p]Now the New York location has been out for a little while and you've all had a chance to really dig in, we thought we'd jump into some top tips on mastering the map.[/p][p]Whether you're revisiting the map or diving in for the first time, this blog will include a bunch of tips that will help you build a hotel that thrives in the city that never sleeps and make your builds more efficient and profitable!
[/p][h3][b]Top Tips for Building a Top-Tier New York Hotel!
[/b][/h3][h3][b]Start Smart[/b][/h3][p]Choose the financing option that matches your playstyle - the New York map has 3 finance options to choose from in the scenario. Risk-takers might go for high loans, while strategists may prefer slow, steady growth.

The three types are: [/p][list][*][p] Investment - starting money $275,000 but you must pay 5 $25,000 lumps starting on day 20 and eventually reach a hotel value of $2.5 million![/p][/*][*][p]City Loan - starting money $350,000 but you must pay back the city $250,000 and at some point have 25 staff hired consecutively for 5 days. [/p][/*][*][p]Bootstrap - starting money $150,000 and you need to reach a profit of $2,000 per employee for 3 consecutive days and have 10 bedrooms on the same floor.[/p][/*][/list][p]Some of these are easier than others, depending on your play style with bootstrap being more independent but less starting funds! Figure out which is the best for you, or if you like a challenge you could try to be successful with a build on all 3 options.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/c556112962dfcc2237941d862854c6b9b50f0c08.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Balance Luxury and Practicality[/b][/h3][p]Offer a mix of room types including luxury suites, business rooms, and budget-friendly options. If you build too big too quickly, then you'll find yourself running out of money very fast! 

If you play with a 'build everything in big chunks' style, then you'll need to remind yourself to avoid getting low on funds and let the hotel function at least a little bit while building. 

The easiest way to gradually build a successful hotel is to start with the guests that require the lower star ratings like Backpackers and work your way up to the 5 star demanding Upper Crust. You can always hop back and upgrade the lower star rooms later or renovate them entirely once the hotel is more established.
[/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/beb5326ad17846b60ad99542245073ce32f6fe4f.jpg"][/img]
[b]Design with Vertical Efficiency![/b][/h3][p]Elevators are quite important in this map - after all you don't want it to take half a day for a cleaner to take sheets up to the top floors!

If you are looking to make the most out of the space in your hotels, once your elevator is built, you can delete the stairs. This will help when squeezing in those extra rooms.

You can also make your layouts more efficient by popping in another staff room or multiple laundry zones etc to reduce travel time of your staff. [/p][h3]
[b]Spread out your zones[/b]  [/h3][p]Remember you have 25 times the 10x10 tiles to play with here, so having an entire restaurant floor isn't a bad idea if you're catering to lots of hungry guests!   You could even spread the kitchen out onto another floor for a mega restaurant.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/746bf248c274ea2548d5de4511dee79de5c299f6.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Problem solving[/b][/h3][p]When you're having an issue with something in your hotel either not being done or a flow problem, follow the staff that are meant to be tackling this or watch your guests as the wander around.   [/p][p]You'll often be able to suss out what's gone wrong by assessing what is causing the problem.   [/p][p]Beds not being made: How over worked are your cleaners or are there enough washing machines?  [/p][p]Trash piling up: Do you have enough dumpsters/bins and do your cleaners have time in the day after prioritising making the beds? [/p][p]Guests leaving because they can't check in: Do you have enough receptionists to tackle the busy influx of check outs/check ins?   [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/3853a75f24c944669577692aa82127f33526217a.jpg"][/img]
You can also seek help in the steam discussions, our [url="https://discord.gg/Hotelarchitect"]discord[/url] or you may find some helpful tips on our [url="https://hotel-architect.fandom.com/wiki/Hotel_Architect_Wiki"]Hotel Architect Wiki.[/url]



P.S. If you read this far, thank you and you'll also be happy to know we have a big announcement on the next location coming next week 👀 [/p][h2][/h2]

notes.title: Guest Focus: Sunbathers!
notes.content:
[p]Ah, the Sunbather. The sun-kissed, SPF-averse, swimsuit wearing guest of your hotel empires. If you’re building a resort in Hotel Architect and you’re not catering to these solar-powered guests, you're missing a trick! [/p][p]Let’s break down what makes these radiant visitors tick.. and how to keep them blissfully baking under the sun in game!
[/p][h3][b]Who Are the Sunbathers?[/b][/h3][p]Sunbathers are the bronzed  of vacationers of your guest list. They don’t care about your five-star dining or your avant-garde art installations. No, no. These folks are here for one thing and one thing only: maximum UV exposure![/p][p]They’re drawn to hotels that offer ample tanning opportunities. Think of the average sun worshipping vacationers that have a craving for anywhere they can stretch out like lizards on a hot rock!  
[/p][h3][b]What Do They Want?[/b][/h3][p]Let’s be honest - Sunbathers are simple compared to Upper Crust but sometimes we jump straight past them because we want 5 stars straight away so here’s their wishlist: 
[/p][p][b]Sun, and lots of it [/b](or the artificial kind!)[/p][p]This means sunbeds to sunbath on! Sunbathers will show up to any location, as long as you’ve got the goods. Ended up in Snowy St. Anton with no sun? No problem - a tanning bed inside will do!

[/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/e751b34b79261d5acb831cde1d98e1fc5baa1890.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/74cab362fbb090aa5e72fb7b13f966bb13adef81.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p][b]A 3-star hotel rating or higher[/b] - they’re not savages like backpackers, after all 🤭[/p][p]3 star hotels need at least a gym, restaurant and a bar, plus 3 star standard rooms. You can see all the details about your ratings and reviews in the Financial overview tab. Clicking on the last critic review button will show you more indepth areas to cover.
  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/6bb03b70fa24724a7bfe9730bf8a2703a9a7caaf.png"][/img]


[b]Bonus points if you have things Sunbathers like![/b]  You may have noticed in the Guest tab of the People Area that sunbathers also enjoy certain items. They will like your hotel more and give higher reviews if they have access to these things in your hotel: [/p][list][*][p]Salad on the restaurant menu[/p][/*][*][p]Surf simulator for some entertainment[/p][/*][*][p]Exercise balls in the gym[/p][/*][/list][p]Guests don't have to have these items, and will use others but they will rate more highly when they have their favourites. 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/d4f460b9d94bcdc7388e5100c5a43d59c5173c0d.png"][/img]
[/p][h3][b]Struggling with that sunbather goal in Santorini? [/b](yes that one!)[/h3][p]We've had a few of you mention that you are struggling to understand why the sunbathing guest goal in the Santorini Scenario isn't increasing when guests use the sunbeds. [/p][p][/p][p]If the guest is not a sunbather guest type, then it will not count. You can click on the sunbathing guest to see what type of guest they are.  See below, this is a backpacker, not a sunbather!

[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/5292c7c6b076da90b172351f225b82ef9c4e1541.png"][/img][/p][p]If you are finding you aren't getting any sunbathers use the sunbeds, follow the wishlist above to tick the boxes for sunbathers to come to your hotel!  [/p][p]To help with this, you can also click on a room, and hover over sunbathers in the right hand side panel to see what's missing from it for sunbathers to stay in it.  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/674dfdcafedb0c82c07121d4dd5b5f0a89e3abaa.png"][/img][/p][p]We hope this helps you under one of the six guest types a little more, and if you want one of these blogs on another guest type, let us know!  [/p][p][/p][p]You can find more info on guest types on our Wiki too! [url="https://hotel-architect.fandom.com/wiki/Hotel_Architect_Wiki"]https://hotel-architect.fandom.com/wiki/Hotel_Architect_Wiki[/url][/p]

notes.title: Early Access FAQs
notes.content:
[p]As it's been two very epic months since launch, so we thought we'd answer some of the most frequently asked questions! This blog will serve as a reference area you can come back to if you need to see things like the roadmap etc.

Please note if you're reading this further down the line from July 2025, this post may be outdated (we will try to pop back and update periodically!)
[/p][h3][b]General FAQs:[/b][/h3][p][b]When will Hotel Architect be launched into 1.0?
[/b]Hotel Architect currently doesn't have a full release date yet, but it's playable right now so we hope you enjoy! See our roadmap for more details on whats coming up to the game soon.
[/p][p][b]How much does the game cost?
[/b]Hotel Architect is £15.99 / $19.99 / €19.99, unless on sale!
[/p][p][b]Is there a roadmap?
[/b]Yes there is, check it out below:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/df6dbd198a9a60aa476b4da48ca3c66ac5b0d223.jpg"][/img]
[b]When is the next content update?
[/b]We will be revealing the next content update very soon. Make sure to follow us on our social media/check out our weekly blogs to be the first to know.
[/p][p][b]Is Hotel Architect single player and/or multiplayer?
[/b]Hotel Architect is a single player game and has no plans to be multiplayer or co-op in future.
[/p][p][b]What platforms will the game be releasing on?
[/b]Currently, Hotel Architect is releasing exclusively on Steam. This may however change in the future, we have seen lots of requests for console and mac. We just can't promise other platforms yet.
[/p][p][b]Will the game run on steam deck? / Why aren’t buttons working on Steam Deck?[/b]
Please note Hotel Architect is not verified but it is marked playable on Steam Deck.[/p][p]The UI is not designed for Steam Deck despite the game running on the platform itself at this moment in time. However you can play with the use of the on-screen keyboard or a physical keyboard connected to the deck. We recommend looking at community control/keybind layouts as well. 
[/p][p][b]Can I play offline?
[/b]Hotel Architect is not playable completely offline - it requires an internet connection when finding player profiles when booting up. After then you can game offline if you wish.

[b]Will there be twitch integration in future?
[/b]The team are actively discussing this, but we can't confirm anything yet.[/p][p]
[/p][h3][b]Gameplay related FAQs:[/b][/h3][p]
[b]How does the campaign work?
[/b]In order to complete the campaign, you must at least complete all the main objectives in each location, which are shown within the “To Do List” in the top-left corner or at the top of the Rewards menu. The other objectives listed within the Rewards menu are optional, and will allow you to unlock all the items for that location.
[/p][p][b]Is there a way to not scroll through and find every item when I need it?
[/b]There is an eyedropper tool in the top right of the screen next to the game time UI, you can use that to speed things up if you have already placed an item once and also there is a 'recent' tab in the furniture categories area.
[/p][p][b]Why can’t I keep the hotel clean?
[/b]Make sure you have enough bins and cleaners around to manage the dirt and litter, especially if you have a lot of guests.

[b]Why won't my waiters serve guests in the restaurant?
[/b]If your waiters are looking for cutlery and there are any table spots without it, then they won't serve guests. Try to make sure you have enough cutlery shelves and the kitchen can cope with washing dishes/cutlery in a timely manner.
[/p][p][b]How do I get more guests of a specific type?
[/b]You can get more guests of a specific type by catering to their preferences. When making a room or placing items, check what appeals to that guest type by clicking on the room and checking the right hand side panel guest types. For example, Sporties love gyms, boxing machines and need en-suite Bathrooms attached to their bedrooms.
[/p][p][b]The sunbathing guest goal isn't going up, how to I get guests to count for it?[/b] 
This goal is designed to target the sunbather guest type only, it will not count for other guests. So make sure you have rooms that sunbathers will stay in, and your hotel is 3 stars with sunbeds! Then you will find gradually sunbathers will sunbathe and the goal counter will go up. 
[/p][p][b]Can I revisit locations?
[/b]You are free to revisit locations any time you’d like by selecting the location and either clicking “Continue”, “Load Game”, or you can click “New Scenario” if you’d like to start it again from a fresh save.

[b]How do I achieve 5 stars on Gothenburg/Santorini if I don't have a spa?[/b]
You will need to unlock the spa zone in Paris and then revisit those locations by returning to the main menu.
[/p][p][b]How do I improve guest reviews?
[/b]You can improve guest reviews by appealing to their preferences. You can check what they like and dislike in the “Guests” tab of the People menu to help cater to their needs. You can also see the general feedback from guests that have already visited and left reviews on the “Ratings” tab of the Financial Overview menu, and use that as general feedback on what needs improving. The critic will also give you a more detailed review after their stay has ended.

[b]My rooms are only booked by one person. Will couples/groups be added to the game?
[/b]The team would love to add couples or groups in but at this moment in time the game will remain single occupancy for rooms. This is to make sure everything runs smoothly while the team continues to develop other areas, but it is a possibility in future.[/p][p]
[b]When is the casino zone coming?!
[/b]The team have made considerable progress on the casino zone, but it's not quite ready to go just yet. We will let you all know as soon as we can reveal things!


[/p][h3][b]Building related FAQs:[/b][/h3][p][b]
Can I build more floors?
[/b]Each map has it's own floor limitation currently, this is not only to encourage different types of gameplay but to help stability and smoothness of your game sessions. The team are hearing your calls for more floors/bigger floors though!

[b]Will you add more walls/floors/items in future?
[/b]The Hotel Architect team are working on bringing you lots of new items as we progress through early access, if you have a suggestion for something, let us know what you’d like to see!
[/p][p][b]Can I delete/undo blueprints?
[/b]Select a wall tool + Hold CRTL while dragging the wall tool over the blueprints to undo. This works on blueprints of foundations and internal walls as well. There is currently not an undo button in Hotel Architect, however the team are aware that this has been requested.

[b]I can’t see what I’m doing behind the walls! Help!
[/b]You can hold the middle mouse button and move the mouse to tilt the camera and/or press T on the keyboard to lower some of the walls to make things easier to see when decorating etc.
[/p][p][b]Can I copy and paste rooms?
[/b]There is now a copy and paste feature for rooms and an eyedropper tool for individual items/walls/floors!

[b]Rooms sizes don't reflect the right amount of tiles?[/b]
Rooms sizes will always include bathrooms in the total, so consider that when creating your rooms as well.


If you’ve not got an answer to your question from this post to find, please post in the steam community or join the Discord and ask in the Hotel Chat channel. [/p][p][url="https://Discord.gg/HotelArchitect"]https://Discord.gg/HotelArchitect[/url][/p][p]The team will be happy to help!

We also have a How To video area on [u][url="steam://openurl/https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2oxQvg7jc1kvt4XbiXFLIjxSOjKcP5Uo"]Youtube [/url][/u]and weekly steam blogs also cover the game in more detail, so head to our news page![/p]

notes.title: Feature Highlight: The New Copy & Paste Tool!
notes.content:
[p]Hey Hoteliers,   [/p][p]This week we're doing a little tool highlight as we know the community asked for this one for a long time!  If you've ever found yourself painstakingly recreating identical rooms in Hotel Architect, the latest update arrived recently and with that, the copy and paste tool to save your time and sanity! [/p][p]While the copy and paste tool is rather cool, we know some newer players might not be aware of it as there's a lot to take in when learning how to play initially. We apologise if you already know how to use it, although if you are an avid user, you may want to keep reading as we made some small but helpful additions in the latest patch thanks to player feedback![/p][p] [/p][h2][b]Where to Find the Copy & Paste Tool[/b][/h2][p]The new tool is located in the room panel on the right hand side of the screen when you select any zone in your hotel. Look for the duplicate icon - this is your gateway to faster hotel creation inbetween the furniture and delete icon. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/73763f011af768d8f71392ced2070ae7e21acb21.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]How It Works[/b][/h2][p]Using the tool is intuitive but here's the step-by-step on how to use:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Select a Zone[/b]: Click on any completed room or zone you want to replicate.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Copy[/b]: Hit the Copy icon in the room panel[/p][/*][*][p][b]Move to the empty space you want to place it in[/b]: Navigate to an empty part of your hotel layout, you can rotate the room to your liking.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Paste[/b]: Click to place/paste. The room will appear as just blueprints at first, and then once the builders have created the walls and floors, they'll bring all the room furnishings in too.[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/2c7d00c20ffd21297ba4aacbd0f04f293bc2dcca.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Recent additions[/b][/h2][h3]
[b]No More Accidental Debt[/b][/h3][p]Thanks to the latest patch, you now can’t go into debt further than your credit when using the Copy and Paste tool which was quite easy to do before and something that we could see players getting easily carried away with! The system now checks your available funds before allowing a paste, ensuring you stay financially responsible while expanding your hotel empire.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Cost will now be shown when pasting![/b][/h3][p]We've added a price calculation when using the tool so you know how much you're spending when copying and pasting to help manage your budget.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Mirroring[/b][/h3][p]The Copy and Paste tool now includes a mirror feature, so for all those decorators that love symmetry, this is for you! The mirroring feature will flip your rooms horizontally so you can make better use of your space and have some funky designs too. 

The keybinds for this are the N and M buttons on your keyboard.[/p][p]
Have you tried the copy and paste tool yet? We'd love to hear if you have anymore feedback on the tool, you can join us in the Discord or pop it in the steam discussions! 
[/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: New York, New York!
notes.content:
[p]Our first ever content update is now live, and it’s a game-changer!    The New York content update introduces a brand-new map that lets you build above 5 floors for the first time, unlocking the ability to design and manage skyscrapers!     [/p][p][/p][p]To celebrate we have a brand new sparkly trailer with another ear worm tune, and all the details on the update below (including some not in the trailer!)    [/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="xdDe_kkrYD8;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2][b]So what's in the update you ask?[/b][/h2][p][/p][h3][b]New York Map[/b][/h3][p]Set in the heart of one of the world’s most iconic cities, the New York map offers a fresh canvas for hotel design. You begin with an empty plot and 3 financing choices in the scenario, allowing complete creative freedom to build from the ground up. 

The map allows you to build 25 floors, which is a mega upgrade compared to the previous maximum of 5 and you have 700+ more tiles to play with than the largest map, Santorini!
[/p][h3][b]Art Deco Furniture Set[/b][/h3][p]Alongside the new map, the update introduces a range of art deco themed cosmetic items and rewards, including guestroom items with 10 colour variations, new stairs cases, a gramophone and more! Whether you're designing sky lounges, high-rise suites, or bustling lobbies, the new items make it a breeze bringing luxury and a bit of the roaring 20's to your hotels! [/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Character Outfits[/b][/h3][p]With the art deco themed items coming to the game, we thought it was only right to add some 1920's themed outfits in for your characters to wear as well. Pin-striped suits and flapper outfits are here for you to dress up your guests or staff in![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Copy/Paste Room Feature[/b][/h3][p]Surprise! One of the most requested features is finally here. The Copy/Paste Room tool allows you to duplicate entire room layouts with a few clicks. This streamlines the building process, especially for large hotels with repeating room types or symmetrical designs. It’s a major time-saver and a powerful tool for maintaining consistency across your hotels! [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Other Update-worthy notes (warning spoilers ahead!):[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added new achievements![/p][/*][*][p]Upgrade all items in zone button added. No more tedious clicking through every item in a room when you unlock the upgrades, although the individual upgrade button is staying too.[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked and adjusted the critic rating for Seating, Refreshment, Entertainment, Spa & Gym. Availability is now based on the critic's actual experience, not just a global rating.[/p][/*][*][p]More new furniture including artwork and other decorative items![/p][/*][*][p]Sandbox is now available directly, temporarily unlocking all zones and basic necessary items 👀[/p][/*][*][p]Added more backpacker guests for those big builds with lots of bedrooms![/p][/*][*][p]Advanced tab in in the Financials area now shows a list of key metrics for your hotel.[/p][/*][*][p]Added queue time-outs in Seating, Entertainment, Refreshment, Spa & Gym activities.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Character Dialogue issues[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issues with chat bubble icons[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed functionality on the bar counter corners[/p][/*][*][p]Stability Improvements + various minor fixes![/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Roadmap Update![/b][/h2][p]Looking ahead, we updated the roadmap to show that London will be a new map we are adding to Hotel Architect in the future! Stay tuned for more details as development progresses. [/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/df6dbd198a9a60aa476b4da48ca3c66ac5b0d223.jpg"][/img][b]Noblechairs Ultimate Cozy Bundle Giveaway[/b][/h2][p]To celebrate the New York update, [i]Hotel Architect[/i] has partnered with Noblechairs and Overclockers UK  for a special giveaway. The Ultimate Cozy Bundle includes a one-of-a-kind Noblechairs HERO gaming chair and cozy gaming gear designed for comfort and style while you build your hotels! notes.title: How to build a 5 star hotel from scratch!
notes.content:
[p]5 stars may seem like a lot to achieve in Hotel Architect! It requires just the right combination of decorations, staffing, and a few must-have zones to truly impress your guests and critics alike.

While completing the Paris scenario technically gets you to that coveted 5-star level, what about doing it on your own - from scratch? That’s a different challenge entirely. There isn’t one straightforward combination to reach 5 stars, and while the in-game tutorials give you the basics, there’s more to the process than they show. So let’s break it down into bite size chunks, starting with your 5-star shopping list.

[/p][h2]Your 5-Star Shopping List[/h2][p]To earn 5 stars, you'll need to check off several critical features and satisfy multiple guest types. Here’s what you should build into your hotel:[/p][list][*][p] You'll need a gym, a bar, a spa and a restaurant for your guests. [/p][/*][*][p] The standard facilities a hotel needs to run - lobby, workshop, staff room & laundry room.[/p][/*][*][p] Some standard rooms to make some money while you're building your way to 5 stars![/p][/*][*][p] At least one Upper Crust–friendly room [/p][/*][*][p] Critic satisfaction increasing with each visit[/p][/*][*][p] Experienced staff to help run your hotel
[/p][/*][/list][h2]Getting Started[/h2][p]There isn't a strict starting point, but here’s the lowdown on how to combine everything above into a high-performing 5-star layout:

[/p][h3]Smart Zoning & Layouts[/h3][p]Organise your space first, lay it out as a blueprint and figure out how many rooms you would like and where. Even thought you might not build it all to start off with as that would demolish your bank balance, its good to have an idea of what you want to build. You do need a functioning hotel to get things off the ground though, so start slow with the basics when actually building!

[/p][h3]Cater to All Guests initially![/h3][p]Balance is key. You need standard rooms for backpackers, Sunbathers, Sporties etc and luxury suites to satisfy the Upper Crust. Start with the achievable rooms, for guests that require lower stars, and then work your way up to the Brats and Upper Crust.

A few rooms with 30+ tiles, premium décor, and luxury furniture will be perfect for Upper Crust - if you are patient, you can do this with just one big room to get that 5 star rating. You can increase the likelihood of a critic staying in the best room if you have a few very nice ones.

[b]Remember! 
Check guest preferences using the Guest Profiles tab and try to please everybody generally across the hotel with lots of entertainment and decoration.[/b]

[/p][h3]Essential Facilities by Star Level[/h3][p]Design your hotel with progressive expansion in mind, move up through the 2 star requirements.
Make sure these facilities are not only present as you build but well-decorated and fully staffed to function at peak quality! As you progress up to 5 stars with facilities, you should already be sneaking towards higher ratings in other areas too.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/7dbbb8bad0455429c8d9f9d2a723b74f9e1f2be6.gif"][/img]
[/p][h2]Staff Makes or Breaks the Experience[/h2][p]Even the most beautifully designed hotel will suffer if the staff isn’t up to par. This can either take time to let your staff learn with xp, or you can fire them and hire staff with higher levels as you increase the rating of your hotel (make sure you have the upgrade tree perks for this though!)

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/a4dcf137af476904b1251f591e2d39a930055218.jpg"][/img]
[/p][h2]Cleanliness and Decor Matter[/h2][p]Don’t overlook the aesthetic and cleanliness layers! These are really handy to see where your hotel is lacking in both departments. Use plants, art, and furniture with high diamond ratings to boost scores, ensure regular housekeeping coverage across all guest areas, and you must upgrade the furniture in rooms for higher ratings too.

Don't forget seating elsewhere in the hotel either, critics will look for this and they rate higher on the more luxurious seating too!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/d891ba4f00ed918c93d2332054974910056ca6b7.gif"][/img]
[/p][h2]Keep an Eye on the Critics[/h2][p]To truly earn 5 stars, you must impress the critics. Your hotel's critic score can only go up one star at at time, so achieving 5 stars will come gradually even if you get 5 stars from your first critic. Critics opinions can vary slightly, as they do in real life and with every hotel stay being ever-so-slightly different. 
You can get an idea of where is lacking by looking at your critic rating at the end of their stay or following them about and watching as they rate some of their activities.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/c2d1019decb33da42035e3eee5185c52c211aaec.gif"][/img]
With this guide as a solid plan, you'll go from blueprint to 5-star luxury in no time! 
If you have any questions or need help, be sure to ask in the steam discussions or in our [url="https://discord.gg/hotelarchitect"]discord server[/url] and also be sure to check out our weekly challenge for build inspiration.

Happy Building, and we'll a nice big update for you soon! 
- The Hotel Architect Team
[/p]

notes.title: Location Deep Dive: St Anton!
notes.content:
Set in the Austrian Alps, the St. Anton map location offers a unique challenge, stepping away from our previous urban and coastal settings in Gothenburg and Santorini. Here, you must design and manage a hotel that caters to winter sports enthusiasts and luxury seekers alike!
So what is different in St Anton?

[h2]Ski Rentals [/h2]
In St. Anton, providing ski equipment is essential. Guests expect convenient access to rentals, after all, that’s what they’re here for! Make sure they can rent their skiing equipment so they can head out on the slopes behind your hotel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/bc7af2289f471c8e073308be4103a739dfb5ecb2.png[/img]

[h2]Mastering Temperature Management[/h2]
The alpine environment introduces new challenges in maintaining the perfect indoor temperatures. You need to make sure the place is warm enough but not too hot, so radiators are key! Neglecting this aspect can lead to decreased guest satisfaction, negative reviews and even a very ice-y death! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/82fb767bfe4b37dac35d62422e98a2a9ca56f1d7.png[/img]

[h2]Introducing Saunas: A New Zone![/h2]
St. Anton is the first map where you can unlock and build saunas. These facilities not only boost the hotel's rating but also cater to guests seeking relaxation after a day on the slopes. The question is, will you go down the route of having the full works with a spa or just a small sauna as a practical zone?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/acca8e0b1d3a48d7e4f27a753f37bf6ecf77a72e.png[/img]

[h2]Hot Tips for Success in St. Anton[/h2]
[list]
[*] Invest in Heating: Just like in Santorini with aircon, radiators in St Anton are important!
[*] Use everything you’ve learnt before: You can choose to cater to a particular guest type or all of them but remember to use everything you’ve learnt in other levels!
[*] Try out the new zone: The sauna is an all important zone in this one, see your guests relax and enjoy a break after a long day of skiing!
[*] Don't forget to check out the reward items you can earn on this map - you might find some cool goodies!
[/list]
We hope you've all started to really get to grips with how your hotels run and we'd love to see some epic hotel builds if you want to share in the screenshots area on steam! We might even run a competition for best build at some point in the near future, so get practising 👀

Also, in case you missed it, hotfix No. 2 is now live so if you've been having some issues with lazy cleaners and low gym ratings, they should be fixed! 

Hope you all have a great weekend and happy building! 
- The Hotel Architect Team

notes.title: Services in Hotel Architect – Construction, Garbage, and Supply!
notes.content:
Hello Hoteliers! 

This week, we're taking a closer look at the Service Systems in Hotel Architect - your last how-to overview before Early Access launches next week! 

In our previous post, we covered the various staff roles working within your hotel. But not everything can be handled in-house. Certain tasks require assistance from external services, which are essential for keeping your hotel clean, stocked, and structurally sound. 

There are three types of services in Hotel Architect. Some operate automatically, while others need to be called in by you at the right time. Let’s take a look: 

[h2]Construction Workers: Building the Foundation [/h2]
You’ll likely become very familiar with this service (or might already be if you joined the playtests!)

Construction Workers are responsible for everything related to building and modifying your hotel. Their tasks include: 
Placing structures like foundations, inner walls, and material sites 
Installing structure items such as doors, windows, stairs, and elevators 
Applying custom surface finishes - from wallpaper and paint to wood, tile, and stone 
Placing furnishings and fixtures throughout hotel zones 
Performing demolition, whether you’re removing a single object or redesigning entire areas 

Construction workers need to be called in when you place objects or structures through the build menu. The same applies when changes are needed, simply call them in! This process is covered in detail during the campaign tutorial in Gothenburg, so you can learn as you go!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/bfdaf4378a26b82214ba2560a95bdec0f82994d1.png[/img]

[h2]Garbage Service: Keeping Things Clean Behind the Scenes [/h2]
While less noticable than construction, the Garbage Service is critical to hotel cleanliness!
Each in-game day, garbage collectors arrive to empty the dumpsters located around your hotel. However, it’s your hotel cleaners who move trash bags from bins and cans into those dumpsters. 
If your cleaning team is busy handling beds, dirty floors or other tasks, garbage might not be dealt with promptly. Make sure to balance your staffing to keep things running smoothly! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/654186582f198a21d12315ff9d400126f5a1d179.png[/img]

[h2]Supply Service: Essential for Restocking [/h2]
The Supply Service ensures that your maintenance staff can keep machines and amenities stocked and operational. 
Supplies are delivered to your hotel and then the maintenance staff will take them to the supply stand in the maintenance workshop. From there, staff can restock vending machines, kitchen fridges, and more. The system runs periodically, but if you’re running low on inventory, it’s worth checking: 
[list]
[*] Whether your supply stand is fully stocked 
[*] If your staff can reach and distribute items efficiently 
[*] And whether you might benefit from adding an extra fridge or supply stand in high-traffic areas 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/ea20b591fe087fab03d8cd71dba05d07d16beec1.png[/img]

Only 4 days left until Hotel Architect launches in Early Access on Steam! Don’t forget to wishlist, and thank you for your continued support - we can’t wait for you to start building next week. 

— The Hotel Architect Team

notes.title: How to recruit staff in Hotel Architect!
notes.content:
Hello hoteliers!
We know you're all excited for Early Access in less than 2 weeks, so we're setting you up with even more info on how to be the best hoteliers right off the bat! Today, we’re diving into one of the most essential aspects of running a successful hotel in Hotel Architect: recruiting and managing your staff.

Whether it’s receptionists, cleaners, chefs, or bartenders, your team has a direct impact on the quality of your guests’ experience. Hiring the right people and managing them well can be the difference between five stars and utter chaos. Here’s what you need to know.

[h2]Staff Roles in Hotel Architect[/h2]
As your hotel grows, so does the need for a skilled and balanced team. You’ll need a variety of roles to keep operations running smoothly, including:
[list]
[*] Receptionists
[*] Cleaners
[*] Maintenance
[*] Chefs
[*] Waiters
[*] Bartenders
[*] And more, coming soon...
[/list]
Each of these positions contributes to different areas of the hotel, so plan things out and keep a close eye on their activities!

[h2]How to Recruit New Staff[/h2]
To begin hiring, open the Staff tab via the People icon on your main toolbar. From there, you’ll see a list of potential candidates for each role, including their skill level and attributes.

If none of the current candidates are a good fit, you can wait for a new set to appear. But be careful, going without key staff for too long can quickly lead to operational meltdowns and unhappy guests. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/4c54884e252b55633f64f360c26d4f11b171b419.png[/img]
[h2]Understanding Skill Levels[/h2]
Every staff member has a skill level that increases as they work. Their initial skill level is influenced by your hotel’s current star rating and any staff-related upgrades you've unlocked in the upgrade tree. Hiring more skilled employees from the start will help your hotel run more efficiently and keep guest satisfaction high.

[h2]The Importance of Attributes[/h2]
Attributes are unique traits that directly affect how well staff perform their duties. For example:
- A Sheet Champion cleaner will fly through laundry
- A Charismatic receptionist will instantly put guests at ease

Each employee has at least two attributes, and both can influence job performance. A “Key Expert” receptionist might seem ideal until you notice they're also an introvert who doesn't do well around people! On the other hand, some hoteliers may enjoy running a hotel full of eccentric characters, like a juggling waiter with the Show-Off trait or a loud 'Shouter' maintenance person. The choice is yours!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/f3335c2ede8e2e37f43bd429243360812fc7f1e7.png[/img]

[h2]Assigning Tasks[/h2]
Once your staff is hired, you can assign them to specific tasks to optimize their efficiency. This is particularly important in busier hotels where managing workflows becomes more complex.

[h2]Experience Matters[/h2]
Your staff’s experience level will impact your hotel’s critic ratings - just as it would in real-life hospitality. If an employee is slacking, it’s worth scouting for a replacement before terminating their contract. Firing a staff member too hastily can leave you understaffed and scrambling to keep things running.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/928557c18fb0977e7f1f7ce033f0f1f000b46a64.png[/img]

These recruitment and management basics will help you get your hotel up and running efficiently. Keep in mind that as Hotel Architect continues through early access, staff systems may evolve based on community feedback.

If you want to learn more about Hotel Architect before the game comes out, head to youtube to watch the How To & Stream playlists! 

[previewyoutube=qfaoGaQKidE;full]https://youtu.be/qfaoGaQKidE[/previewyoutube]

Not long to wait now, we hope you're as excited as we are for early access! 
- The Hotel Architect Team

notes.title: Introducing Hotel Architect Location No. 3: Paris!
notes.content:
After the sun-drenched cliffs of Santorini and the coastal charm of Gothenburg, it’s time to step into the elegance and grandeur of the City of Light - Paris! Revealed as the third playable location, this iconic European capital brings a twist to the gameplay: this time, you're starting with a hotel but it's in desperate need of some serious love and care. You may have already tried this map out in the playtest but for those you missed it, this is the blog to get the lowdown on it!

Paris introduces new zones, the spa and conference room, polished mechanics, and five fully buildable floors of Parisian hospitality.
Unlike the serene sprawling map in Santorini or the structured city plot in Gothenburg, Paris starts with you into the middle of a pre-existing hotel that’s seen better days. Think peeling wallpaper, dirty floors and outdated décor. Your mission? Turn this tired old landmark into a luxurious destination worthy of five stars and glowing reviews.

But that’s easier said than done. You'll need to renovate, reorganize, and possibly rethink everything. from the lobby to the penthouse suite of an upper crust guest's dreams... and all while keeping the business afloat and managing demanding guests!

Paris features:
[h2]5 Floors[/h2]
Paris brings a whole new dimension, literally. This is the first location in Hotel Architect to span five floors, however you have less space per floor than Santorini so you'll need to get inventive with layouts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/d1c40403bb71fdc51539033f69877830ac6401d4.png[/img]

[h2]New Zones[/h2]
The new zones in the Paris scenario are the conference room and the spa. Once you've completed the scenario in Paris, you can then take both zones back to the previous two locations.
In order to achieve that all important 5 star rating, you must have a Spa in your hotel, so those 5 star rewards are now within reach!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/414a8ce37524d161df35a3a9cd88719d18c13c33.png[/img]

[h2]New Guest types[/h2]
The Upper Crust and Business People are fond of Paris and while they booked your hotel as their place to stay, they aren't going to let you slack on any of their demands.

Upper Crust rooms in particular, have to be quite large, so fitting them into the floor plan of Paris efficiently can be quite tricky. You'll need to be inventive while making sure that you have everything to maintain that 5 star rating once you've achieved it. 

The business people while they don't require 5 star luxury, they still have their own requirements including the conference room so they can work while they stay!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/0dbfc5c48feaf2edc1ac15aca284f8e67893c24d.png[/img]

Renovation won’t be easy, and each upgrade affects your hotel’s operational flow, guest satisfaction, and your ability to earn five-star reviews. But the reward? Seeing a forgotten Parisian hotel come back to life under your vision.

notes.title: Zone Focus: Spa & Conference Room
notes.content:
Hey Hoteliers! 

This week we’re giving you a sneak peek at not one, but TWO brand-new zones coming to the final playtest, which is less than 7 days away!  
 
Say hello to the Conference Room and the Spa Zones. These additions are designed to appeal to two very distinct (and higher-paying) guest types: Business People and The Upper Crust. Although, honestly, every guest could use a little productivity or pampering from time to time. 

Let’s take a closer look at how these zones work, what they unlock, and why they’ll be game-changers for your hotel designs! 
 
[h2]The Conference Room [/h2]
Looking to impress the suit-and-tie crowd? The Conference Room is your go-to space for attracting Business People, the guests who are all about productivity, efficiency, and polished professionalism. 

While the Conference Room won’t push your critic score past 3 stars, it plays a vital role in drawing Business People to your hotel. These guests aren’t just looking for a place to sleep. they want a place to work. Expect to see them taking conference calls on their laptops, gesturing passionately at whiteboards, and generally doing all sorts of “important business-y things.” 

Cool tip: Business People pay more per night than your average Backpacker or Sporty guest. They’re a great step up in terms of revenue so alongside sunbathers, you’ll want to bring them to your hotel!

notes.title: How to Attract Different Guest Types
notes.content:
Hey hoteliers - Welcome back to another Hotel Architect deep dive blog!  
 
Today we’re focusing on your demanding guests and what they really want from your hotel. It doesn't really matter whether you’re building your first cozy inn or your 50th ultra-optimized guest haven, either way, understanding your clientele is the key to building a thriving hotel empire. 
 
Now before we start, we do have a short video on this that you can watch if you’d prefer but it doesn’t go into the nitty gritty like the blog! 

[previewyoutube=_eVsu7qWSDc;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Meet Your Guests [/h2]

In Hotel Architect, there are six unique guest types: [list]
[*] Backpackers 
[*] Sporties 
[*] Sunbathers 
[*] Brats 
[*] Business People 
[*] The Upper Crust 
[/list]
Each group has its own personality, preferences, and must-haves. To check out what each type likes (and what they absolutely require), click on the People icon in your toolbar and head over to the Guests tab in game. You'll see a list of their required amenities, and their preferences that marked with green thumbs-up icons. 
 
The table below shows the absolute requirements a guest must have to come and visit (subject to change!): 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/4be3f716d2e75caf5e94c9c5876fd6175623f4eb.jpg[/img]

[h2]Guest Type [/h2]
At first when playing, you might find yourself a bit stuck because you still can’t seem to get a certain guest type in your hotel. There could be so many different reasons for this, but it’s best to go step by step through what each guest wants and needs as a process of elimination. 

If you’re struggling to hit a star rating, for example, Sunbathers require 3 star hotel, then that is your first point of call!  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/ecbef4c5772c132af0a0c051fb8a51d37210e4b0.png[/img]
[h2]Why Star Ratings Matter! ⭐ [/h2]

Star ratings in Hotel Architect are everything. They’re the gatekeepers for which guest types even consider staying at your hotel. For example, Brats won’t even consider staying at your hotel unless it’s got a 4 star rating! 
 
In order to unlock each star rating, there is a facility your hotel much have:  
 
[b]1 Star:[/b] Bathroom and laundry room + 100p 
[b]2 stars:[/b] A gym + 200p (plus previous star requirements) 
[b]3 stars:[/b] A Restaurant + 300p (plus previous star requirements) 
[b]4 stars:[/b] A Bar + 400p (plus previous star requirements) 
[b]5 Stars:[/b] A Spa + 500p (plus previous star requirements) 

Slapping up a couple of paintings won’t cut it; these guests want quality and all the facilities - so make it happen hotelier! Remember your critic score can only go up by one star per visit, so 5 stars won’t simply happen overnight! 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/6c9e1933351fd16f7a83d4daf8e037c0a62cd9ca.png[/img]

[h2]Build Smart, One Guest at a Time [/h2]

The best strategy? Start simple. 
Choose one guest type to focus on. 
Meet their minimum requirements, especially room setups and star level. 
Layer in the amenities they love to maximize satisfaction. 
Once that group is thriving, you can start expanding your appeal. Want to host both Sporties and Brats? No problem = just make sure your hotel has both a gym and a bar. 
Balancing guest types becomes easier once you understand how to overlap their preferences! 
 
Hopefully that clears things up for you and will help you bring in all the guest types when creating your dream hotels!  
 
If you haven’t already, make sure you sign up to the playtest starting soon at [url=https://wired.gg/HAplaytest]Wired.gg/HAplaytest [/url] 
This is the first time you will be able to play on the Paris map and also with all 6 guest types, and it’s the last chance to try for free before early access so make sure you don’t miss out!

notes.title: Mastering The Upgrade Tree in Hotel Architect!
notes.content:
In the world of Hotel Architect, success isn’t just about placing furniture and decorating rooms. It’s also about strategically planning your layout and amenities to maximize revenue, guest satisfaction, and efficiency. The upgrade tree in Hotel Architect is a crucial system that determines how your hotel evolves, offering a pathway to better facilities, higher-tier services, and unique benefits such as speedy builders! Let’s break down the mechanics of the upgrade tree and how to use it effectively. 
 
[h1]Key Branches of the Upgrade Tree [/h1]

The Upgrade tree is broken down into sub sections for each area you can upgrade. 

[h3]Laundry Room [/h3]
Upgrades in this branch improve laundry services, ensuring faster room turnover and cleaner facilities. 
[list]
[*] Better Washers: Reduces the time needed for laundry cycles. 
[*] Better Drying Equipment: Speeds up the drying process and eventually leads to a washer/dryer combo! 
[*] Bigger Shelves: Less room taken up by those bulky towel and sheet shelves or simply just more in the same amount of squares depending on how you lay things out! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/eca2660b3133514f280623c725d35721d87ee846.png[/img]
[/list] [h3]Staff [/h3]
Focuses on your employees, their efficiency and the hiring process at your hotel! 
[list]
[*] Employer Branding: Allows you to look at more candidates when browsing to hire a new employee, 
[*] Energizer: Your staff will lose energy 25% slower than normal! 
[*] Candidate Screening: Means you can hire staff with better starting levels (this has a pre-requisite of your hotels star rating so watch out!) 
[/list] [h3]Bedroom [/h3]
Enhances guest comfort through room upgrades and additional amenities. 
[list]
[*] Luxury Furniture: Improve that all important diamond rating of your hotel easily with luxury bedding, seats and bathroom items! 
[*] Add new services: These were not usable in the demo, however you may have noticed two pretty cool upgrades here including a Guest Comfort Upgrade & Room Service Table! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/dd2544f0181d76d456ddb6466c90c0738e70c66f.png[/img]
[/list] [h3]Financials [/h3]
Provides you with more wiggle room in expanding with loans and credit. 
[list]
[*] Loan Magnet: You will gain access to an additional loan offer.. Doesn't mean it’ll be a good deal 
 though! 
[*] High Staker: Allows you to borrow more money with loans. 
[*] Credit Champion: Allows you to borrow more into the red temporarily, thinkof this like an overdraft. Max this out and you’ll have an extra $100,000 at your deposal, but remember this needs to be paid back and you can run out of money! 
[/list] [h3]Restaurant [/h3]
Focuses on upgrading dining services and food quality to enhance guest satisfaction. 
[list]
[*] Expanded Shelves: For both plates and the pantry – similar to the laundry room shelves. 
[*] Bigger Menus: Attracts different guest types and helps you cater for multiple guest types! Starting with one item on the menu is rather limiting after all. 
[*] Better equipment: Bigger capacity fridges and also better dish washing equipment means less time restocking and more time making guests happy! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/15ef77e620a8ae0fc84b67cddbeac189ff51ce0f.png[/img]
[/list] [h3]Miscellaneous [/h3]
Covers unique and specialized upgrades that don’t really fit into other categories. 
[list]
[*] Vertical Velocity: Unlocks Elevators 
[*] Air Conditioners: A much-needed upgrade for those warmer climates like Santorini. 
[*] Trash In Style: Bigger trash cans, bins or dumpsters – however you say it. 
[*] Speedy Builders: Make the most from your construction crew, now at 1.33x speed! 
[/list]

While all of the upgrade tree is beneficial, you may want to consider which parts to upgrade first and your priorities as a hotelier! Consider your location, what the goal is of your build and also if aesthetics are important to you before jumping head first as each upgrade costs money and time to research.  
It’s a slippery slope, and not all upgrades cost the same!

notes.title: Time for our demo round-up!
notes.content:
Hey Hoteliers,

The Hotel Architect Steam Next Fest demo has officially wrapped up, and what an incredible experience it has been!

We were thrilled to see such an overwhelmingly positive response from players around the world. Your insightful feedback, creative hotel designs, and engagement with the demo have been truly inspiring. Last week, we highlighted some of the best builds from Steam Next Fest, and now that we’ve had some time to review and digest your feedback, we’re excited to share some key takeaways and our next steps for development.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/6388fab7b4acd7590e6b6b037db4e2270268d103.jpg[/img]

[h2]Your Most Requested Features[/h2]

Throughout the demo, we noticed a few highly requested features that could enhance the building experience and overall gameplay. Here are some of the top suggestions we’re looking into:

Copy Room / Template Rooms – Many of you wanted an easier way to duplicate room layouts, saving time and effort when designing large hotels. We hear you, and we’re are working on a copy/paste function! This means you can either choose to design each room or if you want to skip the design part, you can use copy in a design for those who would like to speed build! (Who's ready to speed run a hotel build? 👀)

Eye-Dropper Tool – We also noted the requests for an eye-dropper style tool that is able to select an item/wallpaper/flooring that has already been placed in game. We happy to say we're working on this feature and it will allow you to quickly select any item, wall material, or flooring, and instantly jump to it's location in the menu. This should make designing and decorating your hotel even smoother, less tedious and more intuitive!

[h2]Fixes & Improvements[/h2]

We also identified a few key areas that need refinement, thanks to your bug reports and feedback. Here are two critical fixes we’ve worked on:

Restocking Issue in the Combo Fridge – Some players noticed that the combo fridge wasn't restocking properly. We’ve investigated the issue and can confirm we have a fix!

Builders Not Fetching Materials at Highest Game Speed – When playing at the fastest speed, some builders failed to retrieve materials, causing delays in construction during the Steam Next Fest Demo. We’re addressing this to keep your hotel development running efficiently at all speeds, no need to watch like a hawk for builders getting stuck during your high speed gaming now!

[h2]Notables: [/h2]

Sunbathers - We noted that a few of the community struggled with the sunbathing goal on Santorini, As the term sunbathing and sunbathers is quite similar and all the guest types look the same when sunbathing in their swimsuits! The team have been discussing a way to make this easier to understand.

Icon labels - For accessibility reasons, we're definitely taking the feedback we saw about UI and some icons needing labels or explanations on board. We can't confirm how this will take place yet, but it has been noted!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/23f534fcb0a801a721bad1bfed457f086aea3ab1.png[/img]

[h2]What’s Next?[/h2]

The feedback we’ve gathered from Steam Next Fest is invaluable in helping us refine and enhance Hotel Architect. Our team is now hard at work integrating some of your most-requested features, addressing key bugs, and fine-tuning the gameplay experience to ensure Hotel Architect is the best it can be.

We'd also love it if you left your thoughts on our marketing survey [url=https://us5.list-manage.com/survey?u=f70c3f52ce2e47c5cca7bf5f4&id=33c17aff35&attribution=false]here[/url] if you haven't done so already. This link was in the email we sent out yesterday!

Thank you to everyone who played, shared their thoughts, and helped shape the future of the game. Your passion and creativity continue to inspire us, and we can’t wait to show you what’s next!

Stay tuned for more updates, and happy hotel building!

– The Hotel Architect Team

notes.title: Introducing Hotel Architect Location No. 2: Santorini!
notes.content:
As promised, a deep dive into Santorini before it lands in the Steam Next Fest demo! 

In this blog post, we’ll dive into everything that makes Santorini such an exciting addition to Hotel Architect, from the new gameplay features to the challenges and opportunities you’ll face as you create a luxurious hotel on this picturesque Greek island across 3 floors on a much larger map than Gothenburg!

Whether you're playing in Career Mode or Sandbox Mode, here’s what you can expect when the Santorini location opens up on February 24th (only a few days away!) in Steam Next Fest:

[h3]A Stunning New Setting![/h3]
Santorini is one of the most visually captivating destinations in the world, and this new location fully captures its charm. With its breath-taking views of the Aegean Sea, dramatic cliffs, and iconic architecture, this location brings a fresh and exciting challenge to Hotel Architect. You’ll have the opportunity to design your hotel while keeping in mind as your map is set on the beach front, and your guests will be able to take a dip in the sea!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/aa922e76c4d8e67fd557f0dc75b7a08cf49689b0.png[/img]
[h3]New Guest Types[/h3]
Santorini attracts a diverse range of tourists, from luxury vacationers, sunbathers and more. This variety of guest types means you'll need to design a hotel that caters to different needs. Whether it’s crafting private suites for the brats, or creating an area for sunbathers to tan in those sunrays on the beach. Your hotel must meet the expectations of every visitor whilst dealing with the heat in this location!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/7db79b82fd42fd6bd70b599a932b96ada655540a.png[/img]
[h3]New Zones and Items[/h3]
The new update includes all the zones that came before and a new one, the bar zone! Time to party it up and entertain with a surf and golf simulator and even a light-up dance floor.
There are some Items that are inspired by Santorini’s unique culture, history and architecture, while others are essentials like air con units and fans! These additions will give you more variety to customize your hotel but don't forget the necessities or you might end up with some unwanted guests in your hotel, or worse, bad ratings!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/633b0c36a092ce1dc7de8b17d29a8e91a1af70f7.png[/img]
[h3]We know you've been asking for it.. a bigger map and more floors![/h3]
Building on an island like Santorini comes with different challenges to Gothenburg. However, after learning the basics in Sweden, this map allows you to create on a bigger scale and on an additional floor for more adventurous building!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/72734d8b8825ea5956a13c805600526968d0e594.png[/img]
[h3]The Upgrade Tree![/h3]
This is totally new and we haven't even hinted at it before! This update brings you a new gameplay feature called the upgrade tree. You'll need to learn and research about specific items and topics to unlock better items and improvements such as fancier furniture, bigger capacity bins and combination washer/dryers for towels and sheets!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/b05b013745e8a3ec48b48c164c90f6ae6a79b1e8.png[/img]
[h3]Staff Moods[/h3]
Your employees are the backbone of your hotel, and keeping them happy is just as important as keeping your guests satisfied. In this update, staff moods now play a significant role in your hotel’s success. If your employees are overworked and stressed, expect some complaints.. and even the possibility of them quitting! Staff mood notifications will alert you to potential issues, so be sure to balance their workloads and create a positive work environment to ensure smooth operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/4234d739049f98334b1a2dc81f50b6aa0e72b8a8.png[/img]

So mark your calendars, gather your tools, and get ready to build your dream hotel on one of the world’s most famous islands! 

Wishlist and join [url=https://wired.gg/HotelArchitect]Hotel Architect’s Steam Next Fest demo[/url] from February 24th to March 3rd, and let your hotel tycoon journey take you to the shores of Santorini.
If you fancy, you can join us in the [url=https://discord.gg/HotelArchitect]Discord[/url] while you wait too!

See you all on Monday, 6pm GMT sharp for Next Fest! 
- The Hotel Architect Team

notes.title: Managing your Money: Build your dream hotel, or go broke trying!
notes.content:
From luxury resorts to budget accommodations, the possibilities are endless when playing Hotel Architect, but as with any business, financial management is critical... and running out of money can be a game-changing moment! 

Here’s what you need to know about managing your finances in Hotel Architect and the consequences of letting your funds dwindle to zero, or worse! 

You start out with a plot of land, a modest budget, and an ambitious dream. Your goal is to attract guests, manage staff, and expand your establishment, all while keeping an eye on the bottom line. The game allows you to design every aspect of your hotel, from the layout and room types to amenities like spas, gyms, casinos and restaurants.  

But no matter how beautiful your hotel looks or how perfect your services are, a financial crisis can spell disaster! 

[h2]What Happens When You Run Out of Money? [/h2]

Running out of money in Hotel Architect isn’t simply a minor inconvenience, it’s a potential game-over scenario. Here’s a breakdown of the consequences: 
[list]
[*] Operations Grind to a Halt - Without funds, essential operations like paying staff, maintaining facilities, or ordering supplies come to a standstill. Your employees might quit, and guests will leave scathing reviews if services deteriorate. 

[*] No Room for Expansion - Want to add new rooms or amenities to attract more guests? Forget about it. A lack of funds means you can’t invest in growth, locking you into a cycle of stagnation. 

[*] Emergency Loans and Their Risks - The game allows you to take out loans in desperate situations. However, loans come with interest rates and repayment deadlines. Mismanaging them can plunge you deeper into debt, creating a financial death spiral. 

[*] Reputation Takes a Hit - A poorly managed hotel earns bad reviews, which can deter future guests. Low occupancy rates mean even less income, exacerbating your financial woes. 

[*] The Ultimate Penalty: Bankruptcy - If you can’t recover financially, you may be forced to declare bankruptcy. This results in a game-over scenario, where you’ll have to start fresh with a new hotel or reload an earlier save. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/ba07285ab4dd6b71d5ecc2140f88a97086657b18.jpg[/img]

[h2]Tips to Avoid Financial Ruin [/h2]

[b]Start Small [/b]and resist the urge to build a sprawling hotel right out of the gate. Focus on essential facilities and expand gradually as your income grows!

[b]Monitor Your Budget [/b]and keep a close eye on your income and expenses using the finance tabs. Use the in-game financial tools to track where your money is going and identify areas where you can cut costs or gain profit.

[b]Cater to Your Guests[/b] and their needs! Understanding your guest types is key, so far in playtests only 2 guest types have been available, but there are more in the game to discover. Build facilities that cater to their needs and preferences to maximize satisfaction and your hotel will become more popular as ratings go up!

[b]Take calculated risks[/b] - While loans can be a lifesaver, use them wisely. Only borrow money if you have a clear plan to earn and repay it with interest!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/7c0fa26e6af5f4640173c10ce8b9a53ea6dedbd8.jpg[/img]

Hopefully that's gotten you up to speed on how you can prevent your hotels from falling into ruin!

We release these blogs to help you understand more of Hotel Architect before you jump in, if there is anything you would like to know more about, leave us a comment below and we'll see if we can cover it or at least answer your questions!

notes.title: Zone Focus: Laundry Rooms!
notes.content:
Behind the polished (or disastrous) rooms and service of every hotel lies an often-overlooked but essential operation: the laundry room! 

As a hotelier and Hotel Architect player, crafting a well-designed laundry system isn’t just about functionality - it’s about ensuring the seamless flow of operations that keeps guests satisfied and the hotel running like clockwork.

During the playtest the team found that a lot of feedback said that the cleaners were not cleaning the hotel efficiently. There are a few reasons for this - one balancing and we adjusted it slightly during the test! 
And another management of the laundry rooms and cleaners, which is what we're going to cover in this blog. These tips will help you when Early Access comes round! (or potentially another playtest *hint hint*)

[h2]Where should the laundry room be located?[/h2]
If your cleaners have a really long commute between the laundry room and the hotel rooms. it'll take a long time to get each room's sheets and towels sorted. You might want to add another laundry room in or have the laundry room in the centre of your hotel complex! 
Whatever your layout, consider how long it takes for cleaners to get to the rooms to clean and refresh the towels and bed linen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/e8fc6dfa4ee2dd7e73eb8bfeee3e64943afa9000.png[/img]

[h2]Help - Cleaners aren't cleaning like they should be! [/h2]
If your cleaners are ignoring other areas of their responsibilities i.e. lots of rubbish on the floor or grubby surroundings in the hotel, it might be that they haven't got enough machines/storage to cope with demand of the hotel rooms. There's only 8 sheets on a shelf, so if you have more than 8 rooms, you will need more sheets!

This means they will only be focusing on their top priority, getting those sheets and towels to those rooms and they'll ignore emptying bins or mopping!

Adding in more sheet and towel shelves and more washing machines and driers can help with this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/cea3caaf467377b4241fafe1c7569397c74a9de7.jpg[/img]

We will be looking at the priorities of hotel staff shortly, however practicing good habits will help your hotel run smoother in the long run.

notes.content:
The second round of playtesting for Hotel Architect has wrapped up, and this time it was open to everyone! It was a bit like throwing open the lobby doors during peak tourist season but in a good way - we got a full house of creativity, suggestions, and a few moments where we laughed our socks off due to the unexpected! 

Running a hotel isn’t all pillow mints and luxury rooms - believe us, the construction workers have been working overtime to make things tiptop and let's just say, the guests didn't appreciate the midnight furniture building! Here’s what unfolded, what you loved, and what’s getting the housekeeping treatment.

notes.title: Our First Playtest Feedback & Improvements!
notes.content:
Exciting Updates and Improvements Coming to Hotel Architect!

Hello, hoteliers!

We want to extend a heartfelt thank you to everyone for your incredible support and valuable feedback on Hotel Architect. 

Your input has been instrumental in shaping the direction of the game, and we're happy to share some exciting news: we've already fixed most of the bugs that were reported, and we’re hard at work implementing new features that many of you have requested. But, that’s just the beginning — there’s a lot more to come!

Before we get down to business with what we're working on we'd like to give a quick shoutout to Hotel Architect Discord Member: [b]RafnUnga[/b], who pushed our playtest beyond our expectations and achieved a 5 star critic rating! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/d6dbdd93d50155fd9e2beb8f4be66f938799b16e.png[/img]
[h2]Key Improvements:[/h2]
Here’s a sneak peek at some of the improvements and features you can expect to see in the near future:
[list]
[*] [b]Move Items After Delivery:[/b] You’ll soon be able to move items after they’ve been delivered, eliminating the need to delete and repurchase. This should make it much easier to tweak your designs on the fly!
[*] [b]Improved Cleaning System: [/b]We're refining the cleaning and cleanliness management to make it more intuitive and reduce your staff's overall workload. Keeping your hotel sparkling clean should feel smoother than ever.
[*] [b]Enhanced Zone Warnings:[/b] We’re adding different warning icons for zones, making it clearer when something’s missing—like required items, staff assignments, or a dinner menu—so you can resolve issues faster.
[*] [b]Simplified Item Grouping: [/b]Items that come in different variations (like colors or sizes) will be grouped together in the item list, making it easier to find what you need without overwhelming the menu.
[*] [b]Material Filtering:[/b] Decorating just got simpler! You’ll be able to filter materials like wallpapers and flooring into categories such as wood, tile, and stone, giving you more control over your design choices.
[*] [b]Better Cashflow Breakdown:[/b] We’re enhancing the cashflow menu with more detailed categories and a pie chart that lets you hover over sections to see actual amounts, not just percentages—perfect for more precise financial planning.
[*] [b]Clearer Staff Management: [/b]We’re making it more obvious that staff base salary is tied to their level and automatically increases when they level up, so you can manage your budget more effectively.
[*] [b]Blueprint vs. Built Walls:[/b] To avoid confusion, there will be a clearer visual distinction between blueprint walls and built walls with blueprint wallpapers.
[*] [b]Reverse Capacity Counter: [/b]We’re renaming “capacity” to “fullness” (for example, in bins and dumpsters) and flipping the counter to show how close you are to needing a clean-up.
[*] [b]Important Event Notifications: [/b]You’ll now receive clearer notifications when crucial events—like staff resignations—happen, so you won’t miss a beat in managing your hotel.
[*] [b]More Customization Options: [/b]Get ready for more ways to make your hotel unique! We’re adding new wallpapers, floors, and furniture colors, so you can style your spaces exactly the way you want. [/list]

These are just a few of the changes you can look forward to, and we’re excited to continue evolving Hotel Architect with your help. If you would like to be notified about future playtests, [url=https://mailchi.mp/f1f0e368f0ef/hotel-playtest-thank-you ]please sign up here![/url]

notes.title: Our top 5 tips for keeping your hotel clean and maintained! (Or maybe not!)
notes.content:
Running a successful hotel isn’t just about stylish decor - it’s also about keeping everything spick-and-span. In Hotel Architect, maintaining a clean and well-kept hotel is crucial for guest & critic satisfaction, or maybe you have other ideas if you’re feeling the chaotic gremlin vibes! 
 
For those that want to please those critics with a clean and friendly hotel, here’s how you can keep it spotless and running smoothly. 

[h3]1. Hire a Housekeeper! [/h3]
One of the first things you do when building your hotel is build a laundrette which requires a housekeeper, but they also clean other areas of your hotel too. 
 Each area of your hotel, from the lobby to guest rooms, requires regular attention. Housekeeping staff will clean rooms daily, ensuring that every guest enjoys a fresh and welcoming space. Don’t forget the common areas too - keeping them tidy is key to making a great first impression! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/cc7213cdb45e9968597716f0c711fbbc6e4596da.png[/img]
[h3]2. Keep an Eye on Maintenance [/h3]
No one likes a leaky faucet or a broken elevator. In Hotel Architect, regular maintenance work done by a janitor will help you keep on top of issues before they become major problems!  
If you have a big hotel, you may need an entire team to regularly inspect appliances and other facilities. We also recommend building a workshop for your janitors, this way they will have all the tools they need for the job! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/190ff568d258ca4853d1bfbeff16cfb54bf2fe72.png[/img]
[h3]3. Stay On Top Of The Trash! [/h3]
If your bins are full and there is no way to leave the rubbish in the bin outside, your guests (and staff) will start to leave trash on the floor! This is your reminder to regularly order a waste pickup!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/a5fd3e5712f0f8d88093c90a30c4e452baefe174.png[/img]
[h3]4. Listen to Guest & Critic Feedback [/h3]
Guests and Critics are quick to notice when something isn’t quite right, whether it’s a dirty carpet or a malfunctioning air conditioner. Pay attention to their reviews and comments, and use this feedback to improve your hotel! Addressing these concerns quickly not only boosts guest satisfaction but also helps maintain your hotel’s reputation.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/21e3abb0d4a11aee95a97985a4c62449d8b9673d.png[/img]
[h3] 5. Look after your staff! [/h3]

Staff need somewhere to take their breaks, and certainly won’t work effectively if there isn’t a staff room zone to replenish their energy levels in, no matter their skill level! The last thing you want is for your receptionist to fall asleep at the lobby desk or a janitor to slack off and not repair the items!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/7cbab7a731d3c6e5779908ecb8f9c932c38c31d8.png[/img]
Well, there you have it, our top 5 tips for keeping a clean and maintained hotel, but it’s up to you whether you decide to follow these or turn your hotel into a nightmare stay!

notes.title: Zone Focus - Restaurants!
notes.content:
This week’s Zone focus is restaurants in Hotel Architect.

Restaurants are zones that you can create in your hotels around the globe, however they are optional features you can add. The reason we say zones is because they don't have to be separate rooms. There can be several zones in one open space. 

Restaurants in game are run by the waiting staff, who are supervised by you! Your waiter will see each guest through their dining experience and reset the table afterwards. However, before we dive into that, there’s a few things you need to know about running a Hotel Architect restaurant.

[h1]Things To Know! [/h1]

The first being that you need a kitchen for your restaurant. It will be need to be linked to your restaurant dining area. This is done by clicking the link button when the kitchen is selected and then clicking on the dining area. The dinging are will be highlighted when you select the linking option to make it clear what can be linked. It means that your kitchen does not have to directly connect to the dining room of the restaurant. It could be on the other side of the hotel if you want it to be. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/af17488afc42f85128d4f8c5351441d804b3f494.png[/img] 
Secondly you’ll need to decide what goes on your menu. Careful though, certain types of guests prefer certain types of food!  Each dish may also need different objects in the kitchen. On the left hand side of the Restaurant menu, the requirement show you all the kitchen appliances required to make the dishes on the menu. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/b2e0210dfde75f0b153f264884868d61a4be4d7c.png[/img]
Selecting dishes on your menu is important, you will need to balance the dishes to fit a variety of guests if you wish to please everyone. Or maybe ignore it, and potentially create some angry customers at your own risk!  Dishes vary from all types of cuisine, and have different preparation times as well so there are lots of things to consider when putting together the menu. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/3da926d6025bb7b91babdc5f23d9b586289c609b.png[/img] 
Lastly before getting onto the details about serving guests, your Restaurant kitchen needs somebody to cook the food! Hiring a chef is a really important step, once hired you can watch them conjure up some delicious treats in the kitchen. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/90a638975c39b15a0a980b3fd5d932b58114aed8.png[/img]

[h1]Serving Your Guests [/h1]

Restaurants in Hotel Architect require the waiter to guide customers to their seats. Sometimes if the restaurant is busy, there will be a queue at the host desk.  Your waiter will guide them to their table that has already been prepared with cutlery etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/73bd732c33fadb272260a5c2fa4824941d6327e4.png[/img]
When they have taken their seat, the waiter will give your guest a menu and take their order.  This is where having a wide selection of food is helpful, having something to please each type of guest can affect whether they are happy with the meal or not. If they aren’t they might get angry with the waiter!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/35f6805d75166ea8ee0a49f9ea61400007b8b62a.png[/img]
While the food is prepared and cooked, the waiter will get the guests drink order. This might be a soft or alcoholic drink and serve it to the guest. By this time the food should be ready to serve and on the hot plate in the kitchen. The waiter will head to the kitchen and serve the meal to the guest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/19402d86de7ebcdaf0e601cdfa1d78d924832c99.png[/img]
When the guest has finished their meal, the waiter will check on them and the guest will pay. (Reactions may vary if they haven’t had a pleasurable meal though!) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40373120/480d8289b7f35c49dacc699623bfb648b92c148a.png[/img]


That's it for our deep dive on Restaurants so far in Hotel Architect! We hope you enjoyed and learnt a bit about the depth of the cogs that work behind the scenes to give hotel guests an amazing meal while staying at any hotel in game.

We’d love to hear your questions and feedback on the restaurant, so please check into the Hotel Architect Discord or leave a comment on our social media pages!
